name: Baoshan Washed
tasting_notes: Stone fruit, Brown sugar, Clean finish
description: Rising 1,650 meters above the Tropic of Cancer, the red volcanic soil of Baoshan produces a washed Arabica that competes with the world's finest.
producer_story: A third-generation grower in the Gaoligong mountains, Mr. Chen has mastered the art of high-altitude Arabica for over forty years.

name: Enshi Yulu
description: Hand-harvested from the cloud-shrouded peaks of the Wuling Mountains, this rare steamed green tea carries the heritage of the Tang Dynasty. Unlike modern pan-fired greens, its needles are softened by vapor, preserving a vivid chlorophyll vibrancy and a profound silence in the cup.
producer_story: “The mountain provides the mist; we only provide the patience.” Nestled in the Wuling Mountains, the Qin family has refined the Enshi Yulu technique for four generations.
brewing_guide: Steep 3g in 150ml of 80°C spring water for 45 seconds to reveal its dew-like clarity.

name: Shadow Ferment
tasting_notes: Dark honey, Wild forest, Earthy depth
description: A experimental processing method from Pu'er that emphasizes the deep, resinous qualities of high-altitude cherries.
producer_story: Protecting the ancient wild tea trees of Jingmai, Ms. Lin also explores unique coffee processing methods.

name: Moonlight White
description: Delicate white tea needles from Yunnan, withered under the cool night air to preserve their silver down and sweet, floral clarity.
producer_story: Sourced from the high mist forests of Yunnan where tea trees grow wild and ancient.
